# Svgbob

Svgbob can create a nice graphical representation of your text diagrams.

Svgbob provides a CLI which takes text as an input and creates an SVG image as an output.

## Demo

[**Interactive Demo**](https://ivanceras.github.io/svgbob-editor/)

## What is Svgbob?

Svgbob is a tool that converts ASCII art text diagrams into beautiful SVG graphics. It automatically recognizes shapes, lines, arrows, and text in your ASCII art and renders them as scalable vector graphics.

## Features

- Converts ASCII art diagrams to SVG
- Supports various shapes: rectangles, circles, lines, arrows
- Handles text within diagrams
- Customizable styling via legends
- Command-line interface for easy integration
- Server mode available for REST API usage

## Usage Examples

### Basic ASCII Art to SVG

Input:
```
    +------+
    |      |
    +------+
```

### Command Line Options

The CLI tool supports various options:

- `--background <color>` - Set backdrop background color (default: white)
- `--fill-color <color>` - Set fill color for solid shapes (default: black)
- `--stroke-color <color>` - Set stroke color for lines (default: black)
- `--font-family <font>` - Set font family for text (default: arial)
- `--font-size <size>` - Set font size (default: 14)
- `--stroke-width <width>` - Set stroke width for lines (default: 2)
- `--scale <factor>` - Scale the entire SVG by this factor (default: 1)
- `-o, --output <file>` - Output file (default: STDOUT)
- `-s, --inline` - Parse an inline string

### Server Mode

Svgbob can also run as a REST API server. Send ASCII art as a POST request and receive SVG output.

## Specification

For detailed information about the diagram syntax and supported features, see the [Specification](https://ivanceras.github.io/content/Svgbob/Specification.html).

## Used By

- [google/comprehensive-rust](https://github.com/google/comprehensive-rust) via [markdown-svgbob](https://github.com/boozook/mdbook-svgbob)
- [asciidoctor](https://docs.asciidoctor.org/diagram-extension/latest/diagram_types/svgbob/)
- [discourse](https://meta.discourse.org/t/discourse-svgbob/223573)
- [typst/bob-draw](https://typst.app/universe/package/bob-draw/)
- [zola](https://zola.discourse.group/t/diagramming-tool-integrations-plantuml-svgbob-graphviz-etc/269)
- [kroki](https://kroki.io/)

# Svgbob Server

Svgbob Server runs svgbob as a REST API, allowing you to convert ASCII art diagrams to SVG via HTTP requests.

## Usage

Start the server on a specific port and send POST requests with your ASCII art:

```sh
curl -X POST -F 'ascii=o------>' http://localhost:3000 > output.svg
```

The server accepts ASCII art as form data and returns the rendered SVG.

def svg_stdin(s, extra=[]):

import subprocess, re
def dims(s):
    p = subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable"], input=s, capture_output=True, text=True)
    m = re.search(r'width="(\d+)" height="(\d+)"', p.stdout)
    return (int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2))) if m else None

tests = [
    ("", 1, 1),
    ("a", 1, 1),
    ("ab", 2, 1),
    ("abc", 3, 1),
    ("a\nb", 1, 2),
    ("a\nb\nc", 1, 3),
    ("ab\nc", 2, 2),
    ("a\nbcd", 3, 2),
    ("  a  ", 5, 1),
    ("a  ", 3, 1),
    ("  a", 3, 1),
    ("a\n", 1, 1),
    ("\n", 1, 1),
    ("\n\n", 1, 1),
    ("a\n\nb", 1, 3),
    ("\n a", 2, 2),
    ("a\tb", 2, 1),  # tab?
    ("a  b", 4, 1),
    ("    ", 4, 1),
    ("", 0, 0),
]
for s, exp_c, exp_r in tests:
    w,h = dims(s)
    # compute cols = (w-8)/8, rows=(h-16)/16
    cols = (w-8)//8 if w>=8 else None
    rows = (h-16)//16 if h>=16 else None
    print(f"INPUT {s!r} => W={w} H={h} cols={cols} rows={rows} exp cols? {exp_c} rows? {exp_r}")

            if s1[i] != s2[j]:

            s1_matches[i]=True

# Svgbob

Svgbob can create a nice graphical representation of your text diagrams.

Svgbob provides a CLI which takes text as an input and creates an SVG image as an output.

## Demo

[**Interactive Demo**](https://ivanceras.github.io/svgbob-editor/)

## What is Svgbob?

Svgbob is a tool that converts ASCII art text diagrams into beautiful SVG graphics. It automatically recognizes shapes, lines, arrows, and text in your ASCII art and renders them as scalable vector graphics.

## Features

- Converts ASCII art diagrams to SVG
- Supports various shapes: rectangles, circles, lines, arrows
- Handles text within diagrams
- Customizable styling via legends
- Command-line interface for easy integration
- Server mode available for REST API usage

## Usage Examples

### Basic ASCII Art to SVG

Input:
```
    +------+
    |      |
    +------+
```

### Command Line Options

The CLI tool supports various options:

- `--background <color>` - Set backdrop background color (default: white)
- `--fill-color <color>` - Set fill color for solid shapes (default: black)
- `--stroke-color <color>` - Set stroke color for lines (default: black)
- `--font-family <font>` - Set font family for text (default: arial)
- `--font-size <size>` - Set font size (default: 14)
- `--stroke-width <width>` - Set stroke width for lines (default: 2)
- `--scale <factor>` - Scale the entire SVG by this factor (default: 1)
- `-o, --output <file>` - Output file (default: STDOUT)
- `-s, --inline` - Parse an inline string

### Server Mode

Svgbob can also run as a REST API server. Send ASCII art as a POST request and receive SVG output.

## Specification

For detailed information about the diagram syntax and supported features, see the [Specification](https://ivanceras.github.io/content/Svgbob/Specification.html).

## Used By

- [google/comprehensive-rust](https://github.com/google/comprehensive-rust) via [markdown-svgbob](https://github.com/boozook/mdbook-svgbob)
- [asciidoctor](https://docs.asciidoctor.org/diagram-extension/latest/diagram_types/svgbob/)
- [discourse](https://meta.discourse.org/t/discourse-svgbob/223573)
- [typst/bob-draw](https://typst.app/universe/package/bob-draw/)
- [zola](https://zola.discourse.group/t/diagramming-tool-integrations-plantuml-svgbob-graphviz-etc/269)
- [kroki](https://kroki.io/)

    return struct.unpack('f', struct.pack('f', x))[0]

def rust_fmt(v):
    # v is f32 value as python float
    for prec in range(1, 10):
        s = format(v, f'.{prec}g')
        # parse back as f32
        try:
            back = f32(float(s))
        except:
            continue
        if back == v:
            return s, prec
    return format(v, '.9g'), 9

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import sys
import os
import re
import struct
import glob

#prog name handling
def prog_name():
    import os
    p = sys.argv[0]
    # basename
    base = os.path.basename(p)
    if not base:
        base = "executable"
    return base

# Jaro-Winkler for suggestions (case-sensitive)
def jaro(s1, s2):
    if s1 == s2:
        return 1.0
    len1, len2 = len(s1), len(s2)
    if len1 == 0 or len2 == 0:
        return 0.0
    match_dist = max(len1, len2)//2 - 1
    if match_dist < 0:
        match_dist = 0
    s1_matches = [False]*len1
    s2_matches = [False]*len2
    matches = 0
    for i in range(len1):
        start = max(0, i-match_dist)
        end = min(i+match_dist+1, len2)
        for j in range(start, end):
            if s2_matches[j]:
                continue
            if s1[i] != s2[j]:
                continue
            s1_matches[i]=True
            s2_matches[j]=True
            matches+=1
            break
    if matches==0:
        return 0.0
    t=0
    k=0
    for i in range(len1):
        if not s1_matches[i]:
            continue
        while not s2_matches[k]:
            k+=1
        if s1[i] != s2[k]:
            t+=1
        k+=1
    t//=2
    return (matches/len1 + matches/len2 + (matches-t)/matches)/3.0

def jaro_winkler(s1,s2,p=0.1):
    j = jaro(s1,s2)
    prefix=0
    for i in range(min(len(s1), len(s2), 4)):
        if s1[i]==s2[i]:
            prefix+=1
        else:
            break

p = pathlib.Path("src/main.py").read_text()
# Replace find_horizontal_segments with new version handling [-+] runs

    # Returns list of segments per row: each (r, c1, c2, start_char, end_char, start_col, end_col)
    # where c1-c2 is '-' run (inclusive), start_char is char at c1-1 if exists and is marker/arrow (oO*#<>), else None (if space/text/out of bounds)
    # Similarly end_char at c2+1
    # For now, only '-' runs (not '~', '=', '_', since those with markers rare)
    segs = []
    for r, line in enumerate(stripped):
        n = len(line)
        c = 0
        while c < n:
            if line[c] != '-':
                c += 1
                continue
            # Found '-', start run
            c1 = c
            while c < n and line[c] == '-':
                c += 1
            c2 = c-1"""
# Find the full function (up to return segs)
import re
m = re.search(r"def find_horizontal_segments\(stripped\):.*?return segs", p, re.S)
if m:
    print("found, len", len(m.group(0)))
    # Replace with new
    new_func = """def find_horizontal_segments(stripped):
    # Returns list of (r,c1,c2,start,end,start_col,end_col) where c1-c2 is [-+] run (inclusive) that qualifies (contains '-' or len>=2, not single '+' alone)
    # start/end are markers oO*#<> at c1-1/c2+1 (if any), else None
    segs = []
    for r, line in enumerate(stripped):
        n = len(line)
        c = 0
        while c < n:
            if line[c] not in ('-', '+'):
                c += 1
                continue
            c1 = c
            while c < n and line[c] in ('-', '+'):
                c += 1
            c2 = c-1
            # Check qualifies: contains '-' OR len>=2 (to exclude single '+' alone)
            run_str = line[c1:c2+1]
            if '-' not in run_str and len(run_str) < 2:
                # Single '+' alone (length1, no '-'): text, not line. Skip (don't add as seg, leave for texts)
                continue
            # Check start/end markers (oO*#<>), note '+' is part of run, so start/end cannot be '+' (since run maximal, neighbors not in [-+])
            start = None
            start_col = None
            if c1-1 >= 0 and line[c1-1] in ('o','O','*','#','<','>'):
                start = line[c1-1]
                start_col = c1-1
            end = None
            end_col = None
            if c2+1 < n and line[c2+1] in ('o','O','*','#','>','<'):
                end = line[c2+1]
                end_col = c2+1
            segs.append((r,c1,c2,start,end,start_col,end_col))
            continue
    return segs"""
    p = p.replace(m.group(0), new_func)
    pathlib.Path("src/main.py").write_text(p)
    print("replaced")
else:
    print("not found")
